question.question:
A retailer reports operating cash flows by the direct method. Cost of goods sold for the year is 610000 USD and contains no write-downs; all inventory is bought on credit from trade suppliers, and trade payables relate only to those suppliers. Inventory is 126000 USD at the start of the year and 63000 USD at the end. Trade payables are 116000 USD at the start and 149000 USD at the end. Supplier advances (cash prepaid to suppliers, later drawn down against purchases) are 4000 USD at the start and 11500 USD at the end; cash paid as advances counts as cash paid to suppliers. During the year, 54000 USD of trade payables was settled by issuing the retailer's own shares, reducing payables with no cash movement. Store rent of 18,000 USD was paid in cash. Define net supplier working capital as inventory plus supplier advances minus trade payables, and its change as closing balance minus opening balance, so a positive change means working capital absorbed cash. Determine the inventory purchases for the year, the change in trade payables (closing minus opening), the signed change in net supplier working capital, and the cash paid to suppliers as a positive outflow magnitude. If the implied cash paid is negative, treat the data as inconsistent.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Inventory purchases for the year derived from cost of goods sold and inventory balances
Change in trade payables, closing minus opening, signed
Signed change in net supplier working capital, positive when cash is absorbed
